messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acmecloud.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@datasense.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: inference ops qualification & next experiments

Alex / Priya — great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the evaluation scope and what Redwood will run versus what Acme wants to validate. TL;DR: we'll run targeted quality + regression checks against your current hyperscaler endpoints and the open-model baseline you shared.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary success criteria: reduce hallucination rate on product Q&A prompts by at least 30% while keeping median p99 latency within 20% of your current endpoint (same request fanout).
- Cost target: unit token cost no more than 15% above hyperscaler baseline for equivalent latency/SLO.
- Data constraints: no customer PII to leave your VPC; we'll use synthetic/anon prompt sets for public tests and can run on-prem for red-team runs.

What Redwood will run (deliverables):
1) Delta matrix comparing model variants (redwood-v1, quantized-compat, open-llm-2) vs Acme’s hyperscaler endpoint across latency, token-cost, and hallucination-rate (attached CSV).
2) Hallucination probe suite run: 250 prompts (mix of fact, product, multi-step) with automated hallucination detection + human spot checks.
3) Regression checklist: prefix-caching effects, KV-cache warm start, streaming vs non-streaming behavior on long contexts.
4) Short demo of fallback routing and canary policy (if a variant exceeds an error threshold).

What we need from Acme to proceed:
- Finalized probe prompt set (shared or confirmation to use our anonymized set) — ideally by EOD Friday 2027-07-02.
- Baseline metrics export from your hyperscaler endpoint: median/95/99 latencies, token counts, and cost per million tokens for the last 7 days.
- A small sample of 20 real anonymized Q&A transcripts for human spot checks (PII removed).

Proposed timeline:
- 48h to spin up parallel runs once we have the prompts + baseline metrics.
- 5 business days of runs and aggregation, then a 30-minute readout.

Attachments: acme-vs-hyperscaler-delta-matrix.csv (stub), probe-prompts-hallucination-checks.md (stub).

If that all looks good I'll schedule the runs and assign Marissa to own the probe execution; Sean will handle cost deltas and perf profiling.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[c] +1 415-555-0189

Camila — thanks for the crisp recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifications before we hand off artifacts: 

1) For hallucination detection, can you share the heuristic rules you'll run? We have some internal definitions (false assertions vs vague answers) and want to make sure the automation maps to our taxonomy.
2) On cost: the 15% cap is fine as an objective, but we need visibility into how tokenization differences will be normalized in the comparison. Hyperscaler counts sometimes differ based on tokenizer choices.

We'll aim to get the baseline metrics to you by EOD Thursday (internal export is scheduled). I can provide the 20 anonymized transcripts tomorrow morning. Priya — can you confirm whether we should use our internal taxonomy for hallucination labels or use Redwood's default?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex

Looping in the execution plan. I'll own the probe run and human spot checks. High-level notes for the team: 

- Probe design: I'll split 250 prompts into three buckets (fact-check, product-fact, multi-step reasoning). We should run each bucket against the same seed/randomization across endpoints.
- Automation: use our hallucination heuristics (claim-mismatch and hallucination-entity) but export raw flags so Acme can re-label against their taxonomy.
- Regression checks: I'll include a warm-start test (200-request prefix warm-up) and a cold-start sample set to observe KV-cache hit curves.
- Streaming behavior: run 50 of the multi-step prompts with streaming enabled to see token delivery patterns and p95 of first-byte latency.

All — quick note on the cost normalization approach so Alex has visibility:

- We'll tokenize all prompts with Redwood's tokenizer and Acme's publicly documented tokenizer (if available). For any tokenizer mismatch, we will normalize by computing cost_per_token = endpoint_cost / token_count and then present cost per 1000 normalized tokens.
- For model latency comparisons we'll compare median + p95, and also show a cost-weighted latency metric (latency * normalized cost) so product teams can reason about tradeoffs.
- If Acme wants absolute parity on tokenization, we can run the same tokenizer at their endpoint under a controlled test, but that requires a short integration window.

I'll produce a short README for the normalization steps and include the code snippet in the results bundle. Planning to start the cost-profile runs Saturday morning if we have the baseline export.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher | Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
